documents.title: Universal Guidelines for AI Use in Teaching and Learning: Course Syllabus Template Addendum
tiers: Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution
Permitted for All Activities with Attribution
documents.summary: A provost addendum that urges ethical use, attribution and awareness of licensing terms, then gives instructors three syllabus options for AI: not permitted, permitted for some activities with attribution, or permitted for all activities with attribution. Each option points to the Academic Dishonesty Policy for violations.
documents.stance_why: The addendum sets no single rule: "Faculty members have the flexibility to choose from the following options", which are three tiers (Not Permitted; Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution; Permitted for All Activities with Attribution). Choice is delegated to instructors.

units.why: Opening principle: faculty "should promote ethical use of these tools" when bringing AI into course materials. It is a framework statement addressed to faculty (P56), not a rule on a specific use.

units.policy: Proper attribution is provided when AI-generated content is used or presented.

units.why: Names the citation styles ('APA, IEEE, MLA') that AI citations follow; a citation-format rule, P24 since it names no tool, prompt or output details.

units.policy: Faculty play a crucial role in educating students about the importance of originality in their work and in upholding university values related to academic integrity.
units.resolution_why: A coded course-start/should; B coded general/informs. The source says faculty 'can play a crucial role' in educating students, which describes a role and carries no timing or obligation, so general/informs follows.

units.why: The text concedes faculty "may not be able to always individually verify the originality of all student work". This is a stated limit on verification, not a ban on detection. It is not P39 or P60, which say detectors are unreliable or staff will not police, so it is UNCOVERED.

units.uncovered_note: Acknowledgment that faculty cannot always verify originality of student work (limits of verification), without saying staff will not police.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says faculty 'may not be able to always individually verify the originality of all student work', a real statement of the limits of verification that motivates the next sentences; B skipped it.
